mcqs.question: A drug sold under the name of another drug is called:
mcqs.explanation: Imitation or substitution of another drug makes it spurious (section 17B).

mcqs.question: A drug containing a colour other than a permitted colour is:
mcqs.explanation: Section 17A lists a non-permitted colour as a ground of adulteration.

mcqs.question: The First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act lists:
options: Authoritative books of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani
mcqs.explanation: The Second Schedule gives standards; forms and fees are in Schedules A and B of the Rules.

mcqs.question: Under section 27(a) as amended in 2008, the minimum imprisonment for selling a spurious drug likely to cause death is:
mcqs.explanation: Clause (a) gives not less than 10 years, extendable to life, with fine not less than ₹10 lakh or three times value.

mcqs.question: The section that empowers the Central Government to prohibit import of drugs in public interest is:
mcqs.explanation: Section 10A allows a ban on import of drugs involving risk or lacking claimed value.

mcqs.question: A loan licence permits a person to:
options: Manufacture using another licensed firm's premises and staff
mcqs.explanation: The loan licensee has no factory and uses a licensed manufacturer's facilities.

mcqs.question: Repacking of drugs from bulk into small packs needs a licence traditionally issued in:
mcqs.explanation: Form 25B is the repacking licence; Form 29 is for test manufacture.

mcqs.question: Permission to manufacture a new drug in India is given under:
options: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
mcqs.explanation: The Central Licensing Authority grants new drug permission under the NDCT Rules.

mcqs.question: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act was based on the report of the:
mcqs.explanation: The Chopra (Drugs Enquiry) Committee of 1930–31 led to the Drugs Act, 1940.

mcqs.question: Under section 27(d), the minimum fine for other contraventions is:
mcqs.explanation: The 2008 amendment set a minimum fine of ₹20,000 with 1–2 years' imprisonment.

mcqs.question: The label 'Caution: It is dangerous to take this preparation except under medical supervision' is required for drugs in Schedule:
mcqs.explanation: This caution label is the requirement of Schedule G.

mcqs.question: The Schedule H1 register must be preserved for:
mcqs.explanation: H1 sale records are kept for three years.

mcqs.question: Schedule X drugs carry the symbol:
mcqs.explanation: Schedule X drugs are labelled XRx in red.

mcqs.question: Schedule M of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules deals with:
mcqs.explanation: Schedule M = GMP; N = pharmacy equipment; P = shelf life; Y = clinical trials.

mcqs.question: Schedule V lays down:
options: Standards for patent or proprietary medicines
mcqs.explanation: Schedule V gives vitamin and mineral limits for patent medicines.

mcqs.question: The chairman of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board is the:
mcqs.explanation: DGHS chairs the DTAB (section 5).

mcqs.question: The Central Drugs Laboratory is located at:
mcqs.explanation: CDL is at Kolkata; vaccines and sera are tested at CRI Kasauli.

mcqs.question: The minimum area for a combined retail and wholesale drug store is:
mcqs.explanation: Retail alone needs 10 m²; combined needs 15 m².

mcqs.question: A restricted licence for sale of drugs is meant for:
options: Dealers without a pharmacist, mainly in villages
mcqs.explanation: Restricted licences allow sale of household remedies in sealed packs without a pharmacist.

mcqs.question: When taking a sample, a drugs inspector divides it into:
mcqs.explanation: Section 23 requires four sealed portions.

mcqs.question: The Pharmacy Council of India is constituted under section:
mcqs.explanation: Section 3 constitutes the Central Council; s.10 Education Regulations; s.19 State Council.

mcqs.question: Education Regulations under the Pharmacy Act are made under section:
mcqs.explanation: Section 10 empowers the PCI to frame Education Regulations.

mcqs.question: The number of members elected by registered pharmacists to a State Pharmacy Council is:
mcqs.explanation: Section 19(a): six elected; section 19(b): five nominated.

mcqs.question: The minimum age for registration as a pharmacist is:
mcqs.explanation: Section 32 requires the applicant to be at least 18 years old.

mcqs.question: Dispensing by an unregistered person is an offence under section:
mcqs.explanation: Section 42 covers dispensing by unregistered persons; s.41 false claim of registration.

mcqs.question: The Medicinal and Toilet Preparations (Excise Duties) Act, 1955 was repealed by:
options: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
mcqs.explanation: Section 174 of the CGST Act repealed it from 1 July 2017.

mcqs.question: The NDPS Consultative Committee has a chairman and members not exceeding:
mcqs.explanation: Section 6 limits the other members to twenty.

mcqs.question: The National Fund for Control of Drug Abuse was inserted in the NDPS Act in:
mcqs.explanation: Section 7A was added by the 1989 amendment.

mcqs.question: Government Opium and Alkaloid Works are located at:
mcqs.explanation: Opium is processed at Government factories in Ghazipur (UP) and Neemuch (MP).

mcqs.question: Under the NDPS Act, immunity from prosecution for addicts volunteering for treatment is given in section:
mcqs.explanation: Section 64A grants immunity to addicts seeking de-addiction.

mcqs.question: A talisman, mantra or kavacha claimed to cure disease is defined as a magic remedy under the:
mcqs.explanation: Magic remedies are defined and banned from advertisement under the DMR Act.

mcqs.question: The Schedule to the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act lists:
mcqs.explanation: Advertisements for treating the 54 Schedule conditions are prohibited.

mcqs.question: Under the DMR Act, the maximum imprisonment for a first conviction (as enacted) is:
mcqs.explanation: Section 7: up to six months first time, up to one year on subsequent conviction.

mcqs.question: Which advertisement is exempted under the DMR Act?
options: A newspaper advert for a diabetes cure
A signboard of a registered medical practitioner
A TV advert for a sexual tonic
A leaflet for a magic charm
mcqs.explanation: Section 14 exempts RMP signboards, scientific books, confidential adverts to doctors and Government adverts.

mcqs.question: The CPCSEA is constituted under section ___ of the PCA Act, 1960:
mcqs.explanation: Section 15 constitutes the Committee; section 19 gives power to prohibit experiments.

mcqs.question: In the 3 Rs of animal experimentation, 'Reduction' means:
options: Using the fewest animals that give valid results
mcqs.explanation: Replacement, Reduction (fewer animals), Refinement (less pain).

mcqs.question: DPCO 2013 was issued under:
options: Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955
mcqs.explanation: The Central Government issues the DPCO under section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act.

mcqs.question: Under DPCO 2013, the retailer margin added to the average PTR to get the ceiling price is:
mcqs.explanation: Ceiling price = simple average PTR of brands with ≥1% share + 16%.

mcqs.question: Under DPCO 2013, the MRP of a non-scheduled formulation may not be raised by more than:
mcqs.explanation: Non-scheduled prices are monitored with a 10% annual cap.

mcqs.question: The National List of Essential Medicines 2022 contains:
mcqs.explanation: NLEM 2022 lists 384 medicines in 27 therapeutic categories.

mcqs.question: The Drugs Enquiry Committee (1930) was chaired by:
mcqs.explanation: Chopra chaired the Drugs Enquiry Committee; Bhore, Hathi and Mudaliar chaired later committees.

mcqs.question: The Health Survey and Development Committee (1943–46) is also known as the:
mcqs.explanation: Sir Joseph Bhore chaired it; Mudaliar chaired the Health Survey and Planning Committee.

mcqs.question: The Hathi Committee (1975) recommended a list of essential drugs numbering:
mcqs.explanation: It listed 117 essential drugs and urged generic names.

mcqs.question: Under the MTP Act as amended in 2021, termination up to 20 weeks needs the opinion of:
mcqs.explanation: Up to 20 weeks one RMP; 20–24 weeks two RMPs for special categories.

mcqs.question: Termination of pregnancy beyond 24 weeks for substantial foetal abnormality is decided by a:
mcqs.explanation: The 2021 amendment set up State Medical Boards for such cases.

mcqs.question: Under the RTI Act, information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be given within:
mcqs.explanation: Normal limit is 30 days; life or liberty cases 48 hours.

mcqs.question: The maximum penalty on a PIO under the RTI Act is:
mcqs.explanation: ₹250 per day of delay, up to ₹25,000.

mcqs.question: The term of a patent in India is:
options: 20 years from the date of filing
mcqs.explanation: Patents last 20 years from filing; copyright is life + 60 years.

mcqs.question: Section 3(d) of the Patents Act relates to:
mcqs.explanation: 3(d) bars patents on new forms without enhanced efficacy; s.84 is compulsory licence; s.107A Bolar.

mcqs.question: The code of pharmaceutical ethics deals with the pharmacist in relation to his job, trade, profession and:
mcqs.explanation: The four relations are job, trade, medical profession and own profession.
